item.title: 10 things that happen to your health when you start playing pickleball
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 4.83
10 things that happen to your health when you start playing pickleball What happens to your body when you play pickleball ranges from a fast cardio boost to a real risk of wrist fractures and tendon strain Pickleball's climb from a quiet retirement-community pastime to the fastest-growing sport in the U.S. has outpaced the medical research trying to catch up with it. What happens to your body when you start playing regularly is more complicated than the sport's easygoing reputation suggests. The paddle-and-plastic-ball game genuinely does what its fans claim: it raises heart rate into a real cardio zone, burns a meaningful number of calories, sharpens reaction time, and has been linked in multiple studies to less loneliness and better mood, especially among older adults. At the same time, emergency rooms across the country have logged a sharp rise in pickleball-related visits over the past several years, and the injuries are not evenly distributed — people over 50 account for the large majority of them. That combination is exactly why the sport deserves a clear-eyed look rather than a highlight reel. Pickleball sits at an unusual intersection: it is low-impact enough that a 65-year-old and a 25-year-old can play the same match, yet fast and reactive enough to double as genuine exercise rather than a stroll with a paddle. That accessibility is part of why millions of new players have picked it up in the past few years, from suburban driveways converted into makeshift courts to purpose-built facilities opening in cities that had none five years ago. This list breaks down 10 specific things that happen to your body once you start playing on a regular basis, drawn from cardiology research, orthopedic injury data, and interviews physicians have given about what they are actually seeing in exam rooms. Some of it is exactly what you would expect from any new form of exercise. Some of it — the tendon irritation now nicknamed "pickleball elbow," the outsized share of fall-related fractures, the specific way court size changes joint stress compared with tennis — is more particular to this sport than people realize before they pick up a paddle for the first time. Your heart rate climbs into a moderate to vigorous zone Credit: Canva Images Playing pickleball pushes most people's heart rate into the moderate-to-vigorous range within minutes of the first rally, the same zone cardiologists target when they prescribe exercise for heart health. That is true even in casual doubles play, where points are shorter and rest between them is built into the game. A study published in the Journal of Aging and Physical Activity tracked players with an average age of 62 during both singles and doubles matches. It found that both groups spent more than 70 percent of their playing time with heart rates in the moderate-to-vigorous intensity zone, averaging around 109 to 111 beats a minute over the course of an hour. Singles players moved slightly more and pushed their intensity a bit higher than doubles players, since covering a full court alone leaves fewer chances to rest between points. Separately, the Apple $AAPL Heart and Movement Study analyzed more than 250,000 pickleball and tennis workouts logged through Apple Watch. Researchers found that pickleball players commonly reached a peak heart rate within 70 percent of their estimated maximum during a session, a threshold associated with real cardiovascular benefit rather than light activity. Dr. Calum MacRae, a Harvard Medical School cardiologist and principal investigator on the study, has pointed out that the amount of time spent in those moderate zones — not just the intensity — is what correlates most closely with improvements in insulin resistance and VO2 max, the standard measure of cardiovascular fitness. The practical takeaway is that pickleball can count as real aerobic exercise, not just light movement with a competitive edge. Federal guidelines recommend at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity activity a week for adults, and a few pickleball sessions can cover that target without feeling like a structured workout. The stop-and-start nature of the game, dinking gently at the net one moment and sprinting to return a lob the next, means the cardiovascular effort comes in bursts rather than a steady climb, which is its own kind of interval training even when nobody on the court is thinking about it that way. You burn 300 to 500 calories in a typical hour Credit: Lesli Whitecotton / Unsplash A recreational hour of doubles pickleball typically burns between 300 and 500 calories depending on body weight and how hard the rallies are pushed, while singles play or a competitive match can burn noticeably more. That range places pickleball in line with brisk cycling or a fast-paced dance class rather than a leisurely walk. A study from Western Colorado University measured recreational players and found they burned an average of 354 calories an hour with an average heart rate of 109 beats a minute. The same research found that 30 minutes of doubles play burned 36 percent more calories and produced a 14 percent higher heart rate than 30 minutes of walking at a similar perceived effort, which helps explain why players often feel more worked out after a match than the casual pace of the game would suggest. Singles pickleball burns more than doubles because one player has to cover the entire court alone instead of splitting it with a partner. Estimates using the metabolic equivalent of task, or MET, put recreational doubles in the four-to-six MET range and competitive singles closer to seven or eight, similar to a moderate jog. Body weight also changes the math substantially: a person who weighs 200 pounds will burn meaningfully more calories in the same match than a person who weighs 140 pounds, even at identical intensity. Fitness trackers are not always reliable for this particular sport. Wearable devices are generally built around steady-state cardio like running or cycling, and several device-validation studies have found they tend to undercount calories during stop-and-start sports where a player is sprinting one moment and standing still lining up a serve the next. Anyone tracking weight loss around pickleball should treat a smartwatch's number as a rough estimate rather than an exact figure, and expect the real number to skew somewhat higher during matches with long, competitive rallies. Your balance and footwork improve within weeks Credit: Venti Views / Unsplash Regular pickleball play trains balance and lower-body coordination because nearly every point requires a quick split-step, a change of direction, and a reset into a ready position before the next shot. Over a few weeks, that repetition measurably sharpens footwork in a way that carries over into everyday movement, not just the court. Lisa K. Cannada, M.D., an orthopedic trauma surgeon and adjunct professor, has noted that pickleball is easier on the joints than many other sports while still helping players maintain bone density and improve the kind of balance and coordination that matters most for fall prevention later in life. That combination — low impact paired with constant, controlled multidirectional movement — is relatively unusual. Running builds cardiovascular fitness but involves mostly forward motion. Swimming and cycling are both easy on the joints but do little for lateral balance. Pickleball asks the body to move forward, backward, and side to side within the same rally, often while also reacting to a ball moving faster than a beginner expects. The court's compact size means players rarely have to sprint long distances, but they do have to reposition constantly and precisely. That constant small-scale repositioning is what builds proprioception, the body's sense of where its limbs are in space, which tends to decline with age and inactivity. Because pickleball is weight-bearing rather than a seated or floating activity, it also places enough mechanical load on the legs and hips to help slow age-related bone loss, an advantage that non-weight-bearing exercise cannot offer in the same way. None of this happens instantly. Most players notice steadier footwork and a better read on where a shot is headed after several weeks of regular play, once the body has had enough repetitions to adapt. Beginners often feel clumsy on the court in the first few sessions, overcorrecting for shots or arriving a half-step late, before the balance and anticipation benefits start to show. Your risk of a sprain, fracture, or fall goes up too Credit: Canva Images As pickleball's popularity has surged, so has the number of people getting hurt playing it, and the injuries skew heavily toward adults over 50, who account for roughly 90 percent of pickleball-related emergency room visits. UBS analysts estimated that pickleball injuries generated more than $350 million in medical costs in 2023 alone, driven mainly by sprains, strains, and fractures. National injury-surveillance data collected through the Consumer Product Safety Commission's monitoring system showed pickleball-related emergency department visits rising by roughly 90 percent between 2020 and 2022 as the sport's popularity expanded, with hospital admissions climbing even faster over the same period. Fractures and strains or sprains have consistently been the two most common injury types reported, together accounting for more than half of all pickleball injuries treated in emergency rooms. Falls are the mechanism behind most of the serious injuries. One analysis of pickleball-related bone fractures found that roughly 92 percent resulted from a fall, including cases where a player intentionally slid or dove for a ball and misjudged the landing. Wrist fractures from bracing against a fall are especially common, and women over 60 make up a disproportionate share of them, which tracks with the higher rate of bone density loss after menopause. Several factors explain why the injury numbers have climbed faster than the sport's growth alone would predict. Pickleball attracts a large share of players who are new to organized sport altogether, including many who have not done agility or lateral-movement training in years or decades. The game's short, quick sprints followed by sudden stops put real stress on tendons and ligaments that have not been conditioned for that kind of movement, and a body that has not built up that resilience is more likely to roll an ankle or pull a hamstring reaching for a ball. None of this means the sport is unusually dangerous compared with other racket sports, but it does mean new players benefit from easing in gradually rather than jumping straight into hour-long competitive matches several times a week. Your hand-eye coordination and reaction time sharpen Credit: Jon Matthews / Unsplash Tracking a lightweight, perforated ball at close range trains hand-eye coordination and reaction time faster than most casual sports, largely because so many points are decided in fast exchanges at the net, a rapid-fire pattern of soft shots known as dinking that leaves almost no time to think between reactions. A six-week pickleball program run with previously sedentary mid-life and older adults in rural Utah found measurable improvements in cognitive performance and vertical jump after the intervention, along with a reduction in participants' self-reported pain. The researchers designed the study specifically because pickleball's combination of physical activity, quick decision-making, and social engagement made it a plausible tool for improving both body and brain function in a population that often has limited access to structured exercise programs. Dr. Calum MacRae, the Harvard Medical School cardiologist involved in Apple $AAPL's pickleball research, has separately pointed to cognition as one of the sport's more overlooked benefits, noting that physical activities requiring this kind of split-second decision-making tend to improve memory and recall over time and may help slow the rate of cognitive decline in older adults. The mechanism is straightforward even without a lab: returning a fast-arriving shot forces the brain to process the ball's speed, spin, and trajectory, then translate that read into a precise paddle movement in a fraction of a second, repeated dozens of times over the course of a match. This is one of the areas where pickleball's design works in its favor. The smaller court and slower-moving plastic ball, compared with a tennis ball, make the sport more approachable for beginners while still demanding constant visual tracking and fast motor responses once a rally speeds up. Over time, regular players tend to notice they anticipate shots earlier and react to unexpected angles more smoothly, a skill that develops specifically from repeated exposure to fast, close-range exchanges rather than from general fitness gains alone. Your blood pressure and circulation may improve over time Credit: Nik, Unsplash Playing pickleball regularly is associated with modest improvements in resting blood pressure and cholesterol over weeks and months, the same pattern seen with other forms of sustained moderate aerobic exercise, because the heart adapts to repeated exertion by pumping more efficiently and blood vessels become more flexible. There is also a shorter-term effect that shows up after a single session. Mike Zehner, a clinical exercise physiologist at the Penn State Heart and Vascular Institute, has explained that cardiovascular activity like pickleball works to dilate blood vessels, an effect that can last up to two hours after a match ends. That temporary dilation is part of why blood pressure often reads lower immediately after exercise than it did beforehand, even before any long-term training adaptations kick in. Over a period of consistent play, these single-session effects compound into more durable change. Regular moderate aerobic exercise is well established in cardiology research as a way to lower resting heart rate, improve the ratio of HDL to LDL cholesterol, and increase the elasticity of blood vessel walls, all of which reduce long-term cardiovascular risk. Pickleball's appeal in this context is less about intensity than consistency. A sport people find genuinely enjoyable enough to keep showing up for two or three times a week delivers more cumulative cardiovascular benefit than a more demanding workout that gets abandoned after a month. Most of the cardiovascular research behind these longer-term gains is built around exactly that kind of regular, moderate schedule rather than occasional, high-intensity effort. None of this replaces medical treatment for diagnosed hypertension or heart disease, and anyone with an existing cardiovascular condition should talk to a doctor before ramping up an exercise routine, pickleball included. But for someone without a diagnosed condition, trading a sedentary afternoon for a pickleball match is a meaningful and measurable shift in cardiovascular workload, not just a change in how the afternoon feels. Your joints take less pounding than tennis or running Credit: Canva Images A pickleball court measures 20 feet by 44 feet, the same footprint as a badminton doubles court, compared with a tennis singles court's 27 by 78 feet, and that smaller playing area means players cover far less ground per point than they would on a tennis court or during a run. Less distance covered translates directly into less repetitive impact on the knees, hips, and ankles over the course of a match. Tennis and running both involve extended stretches of continuous pounding, whether from sprinting corner to corner on a full-size court or from the repeated ground-strike of a jogging stride. Pickleball's rallies are shorter and the court is smaller, so the cumulative joint loading over an hour of play is lower even though the total number of directional changes can be just as high. The underhand serve required in pickleball also removes one of tennis's most joint-intensive motions. A tennis serve loads the shoulder through a full overhead rotation at high speed, a movement pattern strongly associated with rotator cuff strain over years of repeated play. Pickleball's serve stays below the waist, which sidesteps that particular stress entirely, even though the sport introduces its own repetitive-motion risks elsewhere, particularly at the elbow. This lower-impact profile is a major reason pickleball has become popular with players managing arthritis or recovering from previous joint injuries, since it allows for real cardiovascular exertion without the sustained pounding that running or full-court tennis demands. That said, low impact does not mean no impact. Baptist Health notes that pickleball can still aggravate existing arthritis in the knees or hips if a player pushes through pain rather than easing into the sport, and the quick stops and lateral lunges the game requires still place real, if smaller, demands on connective tissue. The honest summary is that pickleball trades one set of joint stresses for a lighter one, not that it eliminates joint stress altogether. Your mood lifts and loneliness eases Credit: Canva Images Regular pickleball play is linked to measurable improvements in mood, life satisfaction, and feelings of social connection, benefits that researchers have documented specifically enough to separate from the general mood boost of exercise alone. A systematic review pooling 14 studies and more than 1,400 participants found that pickleball participation was associated with higher life satisfaction and happiness alongside lower depression and stress scores, with the strongest effects showing up among players older than 50. The review's authors pointed to the sport's social structure as a likely driver: doubles play means constant partner rotation, shared points, and built-in conversation between games, none of which is guaranteed by solo exercise like running or lifting weights. Loneliness itself carries real health consequences that make this more than a feel-good statistic. U.S. Surgeon General Vivek Murthy's 2023 advisory on the topic compared the health risk of chronic loneliness to smoking as many as 15 cigarettes a day. The same systematic review that tracked happiness and depression scores also singled out social integration as one of the outcomes most strongly tied to pickleball, a pattern the review's authors said was especially pronounced among adults older than 50 and distinct from what solitary exercise like running or lifting weights tends to produce. Part of what makes pickleball effective here is structural rather than accidental. Courts are often set up so groups rotate in and out between games, which puts players in contact with new partners and opponents throughout a single session instead of sticking with the same one or two people. That built-in rotation creates more social touchpoints per hour of activity than most team or individual sports, and it happens naturally as part of how the game is organized at most recreational facilities, without anyone needing to plan a group activity on top of the exercise itself. Your sleep may improve, partly from being outdoors Credit: Canva Images Most recreational pickleball is played outdoors in daylight, and that regular sunlight exposure helps regulate the body's circadian rhythm, which can translate into more consistent and higher-quality sleep on top of whatever sleep benefit comes from the exercise itself. Dr. Calum MacRae, a Harvard Medical School cardiologist who has studied pickleball's health effects through Apple $AAPL's ongoing research, has pointed to outdoor sunlight as one of the sport's more overlooked benefits. Much of pickleball is played on courts converted from existing tennis facilities or on newer outdoor courts built specifically for the sport, which means regular players tend to get more consistent daytime light exposure than people whose exercise happens indoors at a gym. That exposure helps anchor the body's internal clock to a stable day-night cycle, which is one of the most reliable, low-effort ways to improve sleep quality over time. Exercise itself independently supports better sleep by increasing time spent in deep, restorative sleep stages and helping the body regulate its core temperature cycle, which affects how easily a person falls asleep at night. Combined with pickleball's timing — most games take place in the morning or early evening rather than late at night — the sport avoids one of exercise's few sleep drawbacks, since intense activity too close to bedtime can make it harder to wind down. The effect compounds with regular play. A single outdoor match will not reset a disrupted sleep schedule on its own, but consistent daytime light exposure paired with regular moderate exercise, several times a week over a period of weeks, is one of the more evidence-backed non-medication approaches to improving sleep quality. For players who have shifted an indoor gym habit to outdoor pickleball courts, the change in light exposure alone can be a meaningful part of that improvement, separate from the exercise itself. Your elbow, shoulder, or knee may develop overuse pain Credit: Canva Images Unlike the acute injuries that come from a bad fall, a large share of pickleball injuries build up gradually from repetitive motion, and the most recognizable example now has its own name: pickleball elbow, a tendon irritation on the outside of the elbow that is functionally the same condition as tennis elbow. Christopher Wu, M.D., a sports and internal medicine physician at Atlantic Health, has said that overuse injuries, rather than one-time traumatic ones, are the most common problem he sees in pickleball players, particularly among people in their 30s, 40s, and 50s who ramp up playing frequency faster than their bodies can adapt. Pickleball elbow develops as inflammation or irritation of the tendons on the outside of the elbow from the repeated paddle motion involved in dinking and driving the ball, without any single moment a player can point to as the cause. Shoulder and knee pain that build gradually over weeks of play follow a similar pattern. The distinction between overuse and acute injury matters for how a player should respond. Wu has noted that overuse injuries like pickleball elbow generally improve with rest, physical therapy, and sometimes a brace, and rarely require surgery, unlike a fracture or a joint dislocation. The bigger risk, in his experience, comes from playing through the pain rather than backing off once symptoms appear, since a mild tendon irritation that gets ignored for weeks tends to take much longer to resolve than one addressed early. Older adults who are new to organized sport are especially prone to this pattern because the temptation is to make up for lost time by playing several hours a day, several times a week, right from the start. A body that has not been conditioned for that workload, even one that is otherwise healthy, needs a gradual ramp-up period the same way any new athletic pursuit does. Dynamic warmups before playing, static stretching afterward, and simply building up playing frequency over a period of weeks rather than days go a long way toward keeping overuse pain from becoming a recurring problem.

item.title: What is the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)?
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 4.79
The Securities and Exchange Commission is the U.S. federal agency responsible for regulating securities markets, protecting investors, and enforcing federal securities laws. It is headquartered in Washington, D.C. Created in 1934 after the stock market crash of 1929, the SEC oversees U.S. securities markets and enforces federal securities laws Congress established the SEC through the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, a direct legislative response to the stock market crash of 1929 and the Great Depression that followed. The crash exposed widespread fraud, insider manipulation, and a near-total absence of disclosure requirements in American financial markets. The SEC was created to restore investor confidence by imposing transparency and accountability on companies that sell securities to the public. The agency's authority covers stocks, bonds, mutual funds, and other investment instruments. Its core functions fall into three areas. First, it requires public companies to disclose material financial information — through filings such as annual reports, quarterly reports, and prospectuses — so that investors can make informed decisions. Second, it oversees the key participants in securities markets, including stock exchanges, broker-dealers, investment advisers, and credit rating agencies. Third, it investigates and prosecutes violations of securities law, including insider trading, accounting fraud, and the sale of unregistered securities. The SEC is an independent agency, meaning it operates separately from the executive branch's direct chain of command, though its commissioners are appointed by the president and confirmed by the Senate. Five commissioners serve staggered five-year terms, and no more than three may belong to the same political party. The commission sets policy by majority vote. Enforcement actions can result in civil penalties, disgorgement of profits, trading suspensions, and referrals to the Department of Justice for criminal prosecution. The SEC does not itself bring criminal charges — that authority rests with federal prosecutors — but its investigations frequently provide the evidentiary foundation for criminal cases. The agency was founded in part by Joseph P. Kennedy Sr., who served as its first chair, and it has operated continuously since 1934 as the primary regulator of U.S. capital markets. item.title: TJX raised its full-year profit forecast — but the stock sank on a cautious outlook
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 4.62
TJX Companies $TJX raised its full-year profit forecast on Wednesday after reporting stronger-than-expected second-quarter results, but TJX stock fell after the company's near-term guidance disappointed investors. The off-price retailer's third-quarter adjusted earnings guidance came in below analyst expectations, sending TJX stock lower The owner of T.J. Maxx, Marshalls, and HomeGoods now expects full-year diluted earnings per share of $5.31 to $5.36, up from a prior range of $5.08 to $5.15, the company said. Full-year pretax profit margin guidance was raised to 12.3% to 12.4%, from a previous range of 11.9% to 12%. TJX maintained its annual comparable store sales growth outlook of 3% to 4%. For the third quarter, TJX expects adjusted diluted earnings per share of $1.30 to $1.32. That fell short of analyst expectations of $1.35, according to Reuters. TJX stock was down about 3% in premarket trading Wednesday. In the second quarter ended August 1, TJX posted net income of $1.52 billion, or $1.36 per diluted share, compared with $1.24 billion, or $1.10 per share, in the same period a year earlier. Net sales rose to $15.18 billion from $14.4 billion. Comparable sales grew 4%, the company said. Second-quarter results were boosted by $331 million in refunds on tariffs previously paid under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. Excluding the net benefit from those refunds, adjusted diluted earnings per share were $1.22, and adjusted pretax profit margin was 11.9%, up 0.5 percentage points from the prior year. Chief Executive Officer and President Ernie Herrman said that Marmaxx comparable sales landed at just 1%, while HomeGoods, TJX Canada, and TJX International each achieved comparable sales gains in the 6% to 7% range. "The third quarter is off to a strong start, and we are seeing improvement at our Marmaxx division to start the quarter," Herrman said in a statement. TJX returned $1.3 billion to shareholders in the second quarter through share repurchases and dividends, the company said. For fiscal 2027, TJX is still targeting buybacks in the range of $2.75 billion to $3.0 billion. TJX also unveiled plans to lift its pace of new store openings to 4% starting in fiscal 2028, while setting a higher long-term global target of 7,500 locations — an addition of 500 stores — across its current retail banners. item.title: Deoleo, the world's largest olive oil company, stock surges as Spanish cooperative Dcoop leads takeover race
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 4.31
Deoleo stock climbed more than 20% on Wednesday after Spanish agri-food cooperative Dcoop emerged as the frontrunner in a competitive takeover process, having tabled a €470 million ($545 million) bid for the olive oil company. The sale of the world's largest olive oil bottler is in its final phase, with a closing initially expected in September Although no agreement has been reached yet, the process is nearing its conclusion, with a deal anticipated to close as early as September, according to CNBC, which cited Spanish newspaper El Economista. Dcoop is leading competing offers from Italian companies Coricelli, Bonifiche Ferraresi, and Newlat Food, French firm Lesieur, owned by Avril, and Australia's Cobram Estate Olive. Deoleo, the maker of olive oil brands including Bertolli and Carbonell, reached its highest share price in a year on Wednesday and was headed for its strongest daily gain since March 2022. A deal with Dcoop would bring together two significant Spanish olive oil operations, with the resulting company capturing around 15% of domestic consumption and holding an extensive stable of brands, according to CNBC. Deoleo did not respond to requests for comment on the reports, and a Dcoop representative could not be reached. Spain ranks among the world's top olive oil producers, alongside Italy and Greece, and serves as a global benchmark for prices. The sector has faced dramatic price swings in recent years driven by climate change, water scarcity, and disease pressures. Deoleo said that a period of price volatility has given way to more stable market conditions. Join 500,000+ readers who start their day with Quartz. item.title: Chinese AI firms are tapping banned Nvidia chips through Southeast Asian data centers
item.description:
Source: Quartz Score: 4.29
Current U.S. export controls cover physical chip sales but not remote cloud access, leaving a gap that legislation has yet to close Cassia King, who works as a senior researcher in the Compute Policy group at the Institute for AI Policy and Strategy, said the arrangement complies with current rules. U.S. export controls govern the physical transfer of chips, not remote access to them. "It does not cover remote access to those chips," King said. White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios accused Moonshot AI in July of accessing Nvidia GB300 chips through a facility in Thailand to train its Kimi K3 model, which the company says outperforms most rivals. The GB300 is part of Nvidia's Blackwell chip generation, which the U.S. prohibits from sale to Chinese companies. ByteDance was working with Singapore-headquartered Aolani, a cloud provider holding Nvidia chips, to access compute in Malaysia, according to CNBC, citing a source familiar with the matter. The Wall Street Journal first reported that arrangement in March. Aolani said its services are fully compliant with applicable regulations and that customers do not have ownership or physical access to its chips. Michelle Nie, a visiting fellow in technology and national security at the Center for a New American Security, described the loophole as "threatening U.S. national security," and argued that chip restrictions exist precisely to keep China from using cutting-edge American semiconductors to develop frontier AI systems. A proposed law called the Remote Access Security Act, or RASA, would bring remote cloud-based access to restricted chips and software within the reach of U.S. export control authority. Lawmakers approved it in the House in January, though the Senate has not yet acted on it. Nie cautioned RASA's passage alone would fall short of closing the loophole — while it would establish the legal authority to regulate remote access, a separate rulemaking process would be required before that authority could actually be exercised over advanced chips. Cloud providers are also expected to push back on the compliance burden the bill would impose. King said that with backing from the White House, BIS could produce such a rule surprisingly fast — potentially within days — but cautioned that the harder task would be crafting something with real teeth, requiring decisions about which chips fall under the rule's scope and how to build a workable system for verifying customers. Demand for advanced compute capacity in Southeast Asia is growing. According to JLL, the real estate and infrastructure advisory firm, worldwide data center capacity may hit 200 gigawatts by 2030, approximately twice what exists today. DC Byte data shows the three countries of Malaysia, Indonesia, and Thailand together have 31 data centers of at least 100 megawatts in the pipeline, a sharp rise from the two facilities of that scale currently in operation. item.title: Cape Coral authorities seize 60 illegal slots disguised as bingo
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite Score: 5.30
Florida gambling regulators and Cape Coral police have confiscated 60 illegal slot machines from a local business authorities say was masquerading as a lawful bingo hall. Agents with the Florida Gaming Control Commission joined Cape Coral Police Department officers for the action at Uptown Bingo, at 2708 Santa Barbara Boulevard, Suite 108. Authorities dubbed the effort Operation Going Downtown. When announcing the seizure Aug. 17, the commission warned players that adding bingo branding or imagery to an electronic gambling device does not turn an otherwise illegal machine into a lawful game. “Bingo is fun, and the FGCC supports lawful play,” said FGCC Commissioner Peter Cuderman. “Unfortunately, criminals prey on Floridians by using a bingo theme on slot machines and falsely claiming these games are legal. If you have concerns about the legality of a bingo operation, call our tipline at 850-880-3433. Our FGCC agents are here to serve Floridians and protect them from unscrupulous operators.” Police Chief Anthony Sizemore said the concern extends beyond people playing unauthorized games. “These illegal operations are more than just unauthorized games—they are unlawful businesses that undermine legitimate charitable gaming and can create opportunities for broader criminal activity,” said Cape Coral Police Chief Anthony Sizemore. “Our partnership with the Florida Gaming Control Commission allows us to effectively investigate these operations and protect the residents of Cape Coral. We remain committed to enforcing the law and ensuring businesses operate legally and responsibly within our community.” Players 18 and older may legally participate in Florida bingo and instant bingo when paper cards are used. Electronic devices displaying games of chance, including slot-style reels, cannot legally offer those games. State rules also restrict who can run paid bingo offering prizes. Eligible operators include certain charities, nonprofits and veterans’ groups, as well as qualifying residential communities and organizations. A device can qualify as a slot machine under Florida law when prizes depend on chance, skill or another outcome beyond the player’s prediction. That can cover electronic bingo devices displaying results with reels or other chance-game imagery. Lawful slots remain limited to eight licensed sites in Miami-Dade and Broward counties and gambling facilities run by the Seminole Tribe of Florida. The Uptown Bingo action follows several major Florida crackdowns. In August 2025, Cape Coral police and gaming regulators seized 428 machines and more than $540,000 while searching six casinos and a residence after a months-long investigation. Lee County authorities followed in October with raids at three businesses that yielded another 111 machines and $36,888. Enforcement expanded again in 2026. Operation Reel of Fortune ultimately produced seizures of 623 illegal slots and $350,800 across Duval, Flagler, Volusia and Brevard counties during a three-day operation. Anyone who suspects an unlawful bingo hall, casino or gambling business can send information through the gaming commission’s online crime-tip system. The five-member commission oversees lawful gambling statewide and enforces Florida’s restrictions against illegal gambling. Featured image: Canva

item.title: Fewer Americans gambling as lotteries and casinos lose participants, survey says
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite Score: 5.24
Americans are gambling less often than they did a decade ago, according to Gallup, with some of the biggest declines showing up in lotteries, casinos and workplace pools. Across Gallup telephone polls conducted in June and July, 45% of U.S. adults said they had participated in at least one type of gambling during the previous year. A decade earlier, that figure was 64%, roughly matching results from 2003 and 2007. More than 2,200 adults took part in the latest telephone surveys. Lottery tickets still lead Gallup’s list of gambling activities, though fewer people are buying them. From 1989 through 1999, a majority of Americans reported purchasing state lottery tickets. Participation later slipped into the upper-40% range and has now dropped to 31%. Casino gambling has moved in the same direction. While 20% of adults reported visiting casinos to gamble in 1989, the share climbed to 30% in 2003 before falling to 14% today. Internet gambling stands apart from that broader retreat. Gallup found 4% currently gamble for money online, the only measured category that has avoided a decline over time. Workplace pools have fallen from 15% in the early 2000s to 7%, while video poker participation has tumbled from a 20% high in 1999 to 5%. Sports betting has changed relatively little since 2003, although today’s participation remains below levels Gallup measured during the late 1980s and 1990s. Survey shows overall gambling falls for Americans while online sports betting gains ground Separate research points to strong growth in digital sports wagering. An online Siena Research Institute and St. Bonaventure University survey released in April found 27% of Americans had an active sportsbook account, up from 22% in 2025 and 19% in 2024. Among men ages 18 to 49, 52% reported having an account. The survey, covering 3,084 U.S. residents, found 22% of Americans currently wager on sports. It also identified growing concerns: 60% of bettors reported chasing losses, while 63% said they had wagered at least $100 in a single day. A separate 2025 TaxAct survey of 750 adults ages 18 to 64 found widespread interest in sports betting but limited understanding of taxes. Only 18% knew all gambling winnings must be reported to the IRS. Gallup, meanwhile, found declines across every major demographic group compared with 2016. Participation reached 54% among households earning at least $100,000, versus 45% for those earning $50,000 to $99,999 and 40% below $50,000. Men reported gambling more frequently than women, 49% to 40%. Adults 50 and older registered a 50% rate, compared with 41% among younger adults. Survey method also mattered. Gallup’s parallel online poll measured overall participation at 53%, while telephone polling found 45%. For sports gambling, those figures were 21% online and 15% by telephone. On potential harms, 3% of all adults and 7% of gamblers told Gallup they “sometimes gamble more than [they] think [they] should.” Another 9% said gambling had created family problems. Attitudes are shifting too. Gallup found 57% of Americans now consider gambling morally acceptable, down from 67% in 2016. Featured image: Canva

item.title: CFTC steps in to shield Kalshi from New York shutdown attempt
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite Score: 5.11
Kalshi can keep operating for now after the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) invoked its emergency powers, warning that an effort by New York to restrict the prediction-market exchange could disrupt derivatives markets in the United States and internationally if the platform were forced to shut down. The CFTC issued its emergency order on August 11 after Kalshi notified the regulator on August 1 that New York’s pending request for a temporary restraining order had created what it described as an imminent market emergency. The order directs Kalshi to continue operating under its normal business practices and the Core Principles of the Commodity Exchange Act while the legal dispute continues. The latest development comes less than two weeks after New York Attorney General Letitia James filed a lawsuit alleging Kalshi is operating an illegal gambling business by offering contracts tied to sports, elections, culture and other future events without a New York gaming license. The lawsuit seeks a permanent injunction blocking the company from operating in the state, along with restitution, disgorgement of alleged profits, civil penalties and a full accounting of customer activity. In its request for emergency relief, New York also sought a temporary restraining order preventing Kalshi from offering contracts involving sports, culture, elections and “other events” within or from New York or to people in the state. According to the CFTC, that wording is so wide-ranging that it would effectively prohibit Kalshi from listing any event contracts because the state did not define or limit what qualifies as “other events.” The regulator also pointed out that New York is seeking Kalshi’s profits from event contracts, a penalty equal to three times those profits and at least $36 billion in compensatory damages, excluding punitive damages and costs. The order also points out that New York’s verified petition referenced Kalshi’s publicly reported $22 billion valuation. CFTC argues lawsuit risks consequences beyond the prediction market The commission’s 10-page order lays out why it believes immediate intervention was necessary, arguing that a sudden shutdown would harm Kalshi, its customers and the agency’s authority to regulate federally designated derivatives exchanges. “Put simply, New York’s lawsuit threatens to prevent a CFTC-registered DCM from offering event contracts to anyone in the world,” the commission said in its order. “That unprecedented assertion of state authority cuts at the very heart of the Commission’s jurisdiction and would have significant adverse ramifications for national and international financial markets.” The CFTC said Kalshi’s contracts are used to hedge or speculate on events ranging from Federal Reserve interest-rate decisions and cryptocurrency prices to drought conditions, recession risks and shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Removing access to those contracts, the agency said, could alter the financial risk profiles of market participants across the United States and abroad. The regulator also warned that an abrupt halt could distort pricing as traders rapidly shift positions to competing exchanges, creating unusual trading activity unrelated to the underlying events. It added that markets could begin pricing in the possibility that individual states could shut down federally regulated exchanges. Another concern raised by the commission involves forced liquidation. The order describes an arbitrage trader holding a Kalshi position alongside an offsetting position on another platform. If the Kalshi position had to be liquidated unexpectedly, the trader could be left with a one-sided exposure. “As a result of dynamics of this variety, there may be significant price volatility in derivatives markets and other markets, threatening systemic harm,” the commission said. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig separately criticized New York’s legal strategy. “New York intends to make event contract derivatives waste away under its iron curtain of state gaming laws before the courts get the chance to issue final rulings,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Congress did not intend for derivatives exchanges to be regulated under a patchwork of state gaming laws. These are financial exchanges that offer financial instruments and operate across state lines. “They match the bid from a resident of one state with the offer of a resident from another state and submit the trade to a clearinghouse that backstops the transactions of customers throughout the country. New York has no business regulating these interstate financial markets. The Commission is required by law to ensure order in these markets, and that is what we have done today.” New York escalates pressure on Kalshi On August 6, state investigators with the New York State Gaming Commission issued document subpoenas to Kalshi Inc. and KalshiEX LLC seeking records related to sports-event contracts, including transactions involving people under the age of 21. According to legal analyst Daniel Wallach, the subpoenas are limited to sports contracts and represent the first known government subpoena directed at Kalshi. Wallach said the requests seek records concerning Kalshi’s sports offerings, corporate structure and ownership, and suggested they help explain why the company quickly removed New York’s lawsuit to federal court after it was filed on July 31. The subpoenas require Kalshi to produce the requested records by August 14 as the Gaming Commission continues its investigation. New York maintains that Kalshi’s products are gambling rather than federally protected financial derivatives and argues the company has ignored state gaming laws despite earlier enforcement efforts, including a cease-and-desist order issued in 2025. Kalshi removed the case to federal court on the same day the lawsuit was filed. A New York judge later ruled the state’s request for immediate injunctive relief was moot because of the removal, leaving the federal court to determine the next steps while the Gaming Commission’s separate investigation continues. The CFTC’s August 11 emergency order remains in effect while the litigation proceeds and directs Kalshi to continue performing its exchange functions under its normal practices and the Commodity Exchange Act’s Core Principles. Featured image: Kalshi / Canva

item.title: Seneca Niagara plans $47M hotel overhaul across 22 floors through 2027
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite Score: 4.69
A $47 million overhaul of nearly every hotel room at Seneca Niagara Resort & Casino is set to get underway this fall and run through late 2027. Starting in October, the Niagara Falls, New York, property will update 594 rooms and suites spread over 22 floors. Seneca Resorts & Casinos says the work will encompass roughly 394,000 square feet. Rather than closing all the affected rooms at once, crews will move through the hotel in three-floor groups. The company has targeted December 2027 for completion. “Seneca Niagara Resort & Casino is the gateway to bold, distinctive and memorable experiences for our guests,” said Seneca Resorts & Casinos President and CEO Kevin Nephew. “With this latest evolution, we continue to elevate our world-class atmosphere and keep Seneca Niagara at the leading edge of luxury to make each stay with us even more memorable.” The investment follows a busy period for the hotel, which attracts visitors from the U.S., Canada and elsewhere. More than 181,000 rooms were occupied during 2025, while roughly 141,000 had already been occupied in 2026 when the project was announced. Seneca Niagara investment expands as regional economic impact approaches $2 billion With 604 rooms and suites overall, the Seneca Niagara hotel rises 26 stories. The property has also held a AAA Four Diamond Award every year since 2006. Beyond lodging, guests have access to restaurants, the Spa at Seneca, an indoor pool, fitness facilities, shops and spaces for meetings and banquets. The Seneca Niagara Event Center can accommodate 2,300 people. “Our vision for this project delivers on the elegance and quality our guests have come to expect from each visit to Seneca Niagara Resort & Casino, building on the transformative experience that greets them when they arrive and carrying that feeling of excitement and anticipation of what’s to come throughout the hotel,” said Hicham Jaddoud, Senior Vice President of Resort Operations, Seneca Resorts & Casinos. The hotel work is part of wider investment activity across Seneca Resorts & Casinos. Earlier in 2026, a $2.7 million renovation of Seneca Café at Seneca Allegany Resort & Casino wrapped up. A separate $5.8 million overhaul of that property’s Thunder Mountain Buffet is due to finish in November. Plans for further projects at Seneca Niagara, Seneca Allegany and Seneca Buffalo Creek Casino are also being developed for the coming years. The investments sit within the Seneca Nation’s wider regional economic footprint. An independent report cited in October 2025 put the Nation’s statewide economic output at $1.95 billion, supporting more than 8,000 jobs and $542.7 million in wages. It also identified $365.9 million in taxes and other government payments and ranked the Nation as Western New York’s 12th-largest employer. Casino finances remain important locally. The Seneca Nation’s gaming compact with New York expired at the end of 2023, disrupting casino-related funding for some Niagara Falls organizations even after the city received a $7.6 million advance payment in 2024. “We’re working on an exciting new chapter,” said Allie R. George, Chairman of the Seneca Gaming Corporation Board of Directors. “The projects we are considering at each property are designed to maximize what makes each Seneca Resorts & Casinos property a unique, world-class destination.” Featured image: Tia Wheeler via Flickr / CC BY-NC-ND 2.0

item.title: FlightAware sues Kalshi, Nasdaq partnership announced, today in prediction market news LIVE
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite Score: 4.51
Today in prediction market news, we’re following another busy day for Kalshi, including its appeal of a Connecticut federal court ruling, a new trademark lawsuit from FlightAware, and a partnership with Nasdaq. We’ll also track the CFTC’s upcoming Innovation Advisory Committee meeting, ProphetX and Pikkit teaming up on regulated sports prediction markets, and breaking developments across prediction markets, regulation, elections, crypto, and sports event trading throughout the day. Kalshi takes legal fights to Second Circuit Prediction market attorney Daniel Wallach points out that the Second Circuit has two Kalshi appeals to consider, with cases from New York and Connecticut now heading its way. Crucially, the district courts in both states have so far reached broadly aligned conclusions. That contrasts with the Sixth Circuit, where rulings involving Ohio and Tennessee have created an intra-circuit split. There are now two Second Circuit appeals involving Kalshi, but unlike the 6th Circuit intra-circuit split (OH & TN), the two district court opinions (NY & CT) are in complete harmony. Only other CA2 state is Vermont, which is not yet in litigation with Kalshi or any other PM. https://t.co/XnvVqn3H9g — Daniel Wallach (@WALLACHLEGAL) August 11, 2026 Senators tell CFTC to extinguish wildfire markets A group of eight Democratic senators, led by Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla, is pressing CFTC Chair Michael Selig to rein in event contracts tied to wildfires, warning they could create public safety risks and some particularly uncomfortable incentives. Their letter points to more than $1.2 million wagered on Polymarket around the devastating Palisades and Eaton fires in January 2025. The senators argue wildfire contracts could potentially incentivize people to influence fires while also raising insider-trading concerns. It states: "By offering contracts on fires, prediction market sites run the risk of encouraging people to influence fires that have already started, creating additional concerns around public safety and insider trading." They want to know whether the CFTC could prohibit federally regulated exchanges from offering wildfire contracts and what, if anything, it intends to do about similar markets offered offshore. The senators have given Selig until August 14 to respond. ProphetX and Pikkit team up on sports predictions ProphetX is putting its federally regulated sports prediction markets in front of a considerably bigger crowd. The CFTC-regulated exchange has partnered with sports tracking and analytics platform Pikkit, giving its community of hundreds of thousands of sports fans access to ProphetX event contracts directly through Pikkit. Markets will initially cover the NFL, NBA and international soccer, with more contracts expected later. The partnership is another step in ProphetX’s B2B expansion, effectively supplying the prediction market plumbing while Pikkit brings the audience. "Pikkit's community is made up of the most engaged traders in the country — people who track every result and know exactly where their edge comes from. That's exactly who prediction markets were built for. Partnering with Pikkit gives that community direct access to a federal exchange where the crowd sets the price and every participant competes on a level playing field, instead of against the house." — Jake Benzaquen, Co-Founder and Chief Commercial Officer, ProphetX Prediction market heavyweights get a seat at CFTC table Prediction markets won’t exactly be short of friends in the room when the CFTC’s new Innovation Advisory Committee gets down to business. Chairman Michael Selig has announced the committee’s inaugural meeting for August 20 in Washington, describing its role as helping the regulator navigate the increasingly busy intersection of technology, finance, law and policy. And the membership reads like a prediction market industry Christmas card. As industry observer Matt Rybaltowski notes, it includes figures associated with Kalshi, Polymarket, DraftKings, Robinhood, CME Group, Crypto.com, Nasdaq, Gemini and Coinbase. The meeting begins at 1 p.m. ET and will be livestreamed by the CFTC. On August 20, the @CFTC will convene a meeting of some of America’s greatest innovators, builders, thinkers, and entrepreneurs in Washington, DC for a series of conversations on the future of our financial markets. Mark your calendars for the inaugural Innovation Advisory… https://t.co/4YrPBSysw2 Kalshi calls in Nasdaq to watch the watchers The system will be rolled out in phases and is designed to detect market manipulation, insider trading and other suspicious activity in real time. It will also help Kalshi deliver trading data to the CFTC in the regulator’s required format. Nasdaq says its surveillance technology already serves more than 50 exchanges and 20 international regulators. This is exactly the kind of solution I love working on — Kalshi integrating with institutional finance. Nasdaq is the gold standard in market surveillance, and for any financial institution building a compliance system for trading on Kalshi, this is a system that can power it. — robertjdenault (@robertjdenault) August 10, 2026 Connecticut tells Kalshi: no injunction for you Kalshi’s legal road trip has hit another pothole, this time in Connecticut. A federal judge has rejected the prediction market operator’s request for a preliminary injunction that would have stopped Connecticut regulators from enforcing state gambling laws against its sports event contracts while the wider case plays out. Kalshi argues its contracts are federally regulated by the CFTC and that the Commodity Exchange Act preempts state gambling rules. Judge Vernon Oliver wasn’t persuaded that Kalshi had shown it was likely to win on those arguments. Kalshi isn’t packing up just yet: it has already appealed the decision to the Second Circuit. So, once again, the prediction market industry’s hottest market might just be “Which court gets the final word?” FlightAware wants Kalshi’s cancellation market grounded The aviation tracking company has sued Kalshi, accusing the prediction market operator of using its flight data, name and trademarks without permission to run and settle cancellation markets. FlightAware alleges Kalshi continued using its information even after being told to stop, while also arguing the markets created confusion over whether the two companies were working together. It’s another legal headache for Kalshi, which already has plenty of court dates on its itinerary. Follow today’s live blog for this and everything else taking off in prediction markets. item.title: Washington judge orders Kalshi to restrict prediction markets across state operations
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite Score: 4.36
A Washington judge has imposed new limits on Kalshi, giving the prediction market operator firm deadlines to stop people in the state from buying contracts linked to sports, elections, politics and other topics. King County Superior Court Judge John McHale signed the amended preliminary injunction on August 12. He had previously concluded that Washington was likely to prove Kalshi was violating state gambling and consumer protection laws. “This victory is the first step toward holding Kalshi accountable for their brazen violations of Washington law,” Attorney General Nick Brown said after the court initially granted the preliminary injunction in July. “Kalshi padded their pockets as they promoted illegal betting on sports, elections, the total number of measles cases this year, what will witnesses say during a child trafficking hearing, and even natural disasters.” He added in his most recent statement: “As this case moves forward, we will continue to enforce Washington law and hold Kalshi accountable for misleading consumers.” On Kalshi, customers purchase “yes” or “no” contracts predicting how future events will turn out. Winning contracts pay out, losing customers forfeit their wagers, and Kalshi earns transaction fees. Washington argues those transactions amount to gambling, despite Kalshi describing itself as a prediction market. The dispute follows a December 2025 Washington State Gambling Commission warning that event-based contracts were unauthorized in the state. The commission said legal sports wagering remained available at tribal casinos. Washington users face tighter limits on Kalshi contracts McHale’s latest order requires Kalshi to introduce IP-address and residency geofencing by August 19. A multi-source GeoComply system must follow by September 2, blocking people physically inside Washington from purchasing contracts covered by the injunction. Existing positions can still be closed. Missing the September 2 deadline could cost Kalshi $120,000 for every additional day unless it submits a sworn affidavit explaining the delay. The court can impose penalties if Kalshi fails to show sufficient diligence. Restricted categories include sports, elections, politics, entertainment, culture, technology, science and “mentions” contracts based on whether certain words or phrases are spoken. Commodities, climate, economics and finance contracts remain outside that restriction. Kalshi must also stop targeting Washington residents with advertising for prohibited products. The jurisdiction fight has moved between courts. Kalshi removed Washington’s March lawsuit to federal court, describing itself as a federally regulated derivatives exchange overseen by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. After the case was remanded, Kalshi sought a federal pause in May while pursuing an appeal. McHale rejected Kalshi’s federal preemption argument. “Regulation of gambling and regulation of futures markets are different fields of regulation,” the order says. It also concludes that “The Commodity Exchange Act (CEA) does not preempt Washington State gambling law.” Advertising also drew scrutiny. “Kalshi’s advertisements that it offers ‘legal betting’ in Washington state are likely to mislead a reasonable consumer that such gambling activities are legal under state law,” McHale wrote. “The public interests at stake and potential harm to consumers in the continued operation of Kalshi’s online gambling activities in the State of Washington outweigh harm to Kalshi,” McHale wrote. Kalshi must preserve Washington customer records, including account activity, communications, location findings and marketing information. Washington users can still close accounts and withdraw their money. Featured image: Kalshi / Canva

item.title: Washington and Crypto.com pause litigation, new federal bill targets wildfire markets, today in prediction market news LIVE
item.description:

Today in prediction market news, we’re following fresh legal and regulatory developments, including Washington and Crypto.com agreeing to pause their litigation pending a Ninth Circuit ruling, Connecticut urging the Second Circuit to deny Kalshi interim relief, and a new federal bill seeking to ban prediction markets on wildfires. We’re also tracking prediction market executives sitting out today’s White House meeting, questions surrounding Kalshi’s recently announced Catalist Sports partnership after related pages disappeared, and the latest developments across prediction markets, regulation, crypto, and sports event trading throughout the day. South Korea blocks Polymarket over gambling concerns The move adds South Korea to the growing list of jurisdictions wrestling with the question of whether prediction markets are financial products, gambling, or something inconveniently in between. Crypto.com’s prediction markets are heading for institutional trading desks Trading Technologies says its institutional trading platform will add connectivity to OG.com, Crypto.com’s CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse. That means TT clients — including banks, hedge funds, proprietary traders and other professional market participants — will be able to access OG.com’s prediction markets through their existing trading workflows. Crypto.com executive Steve Humenik says the deal is about bringing regulated prediction products directly to institutional participants as the sector matures. "As regulated prediction markets and digital asset derivatives continue to mature, providing institutional participants with secure, compliant and seamless access is paramount. Partnering with Trading Technologies allows us to effectively bring OG.com's innovative prediction markets products directly into the workflows of the world's leading market participants." - Steve Humenik, Chief Legal Officer of OG.com and EVP of Crypto.com Kalshi’s $40 billion valuation is ‘staggering’ — and betting big on legal wins Kalshi may be in the business of pricing uncertainty, but its reported $40 billion valuation apparently leaves little room for regulatory disaster. Vanderbilt Law professor Yesha Yadav told Bloomberg the figure is “staggering,” pointing to explosive prediction market volumes while warning that serious legal questions still hang over the industry. Those include state battles that could ultimately reach the Supreme Court. Yadav says Kalshi’s bigger ambition is becoming part of Wall Street’s pricing and hedging infrastructure, with its push into perpetual futures helping broaden the business beyond prediction markets. As for the CFTC ordering Kalshi to keep operating despite New York’s objections? Yadav called the use of rarely deployed emergency powers “arguably extraordinary.” Kalshi takes aim at traditional exchanges with stock index perpetuals As mentioned, Kalshi filed with the CFTC to launch equity index perpetual futures. However, unlike conventional futures, perpetuals don’t expire, meaning traders can maintain leveraged long or short exposure without continually rolling contracts. There’s an important correction to the initial reports: Reuters originally identified the filing as involving the S&P 500, but later clarified that it concerns a stock index and removed the S&P 500 reference. Prediction markets were apparently just the opening act. Wall Street, meet the new neighbor. Kalshi eyes perpetual futures as ‘trade anything’ ambitions grow Kalshi apparently isn’t content with prediction markets alone. The company has filed with the CFTC to list equity index perpetual futures, according to journalist Nick Devor, with copper also joining the menu. Single-stock perpetuals aren’t coming “at this time,” but that qualifier is doing some heavy lifting. Devor points to Kalshi’s ambition to eventually offer 15-minute single-stock markets, with product chief Tarek Mansour previously describing them as a natural fit for the company’s vision of letting users trade practically anything, on any timeframe. Prediction markets, futures, stocks, copper — at this rate, the question may soon be what Kalshi doesn’t want people trading. Inbox: @Kalshi files with CFTC to list equity index perpetual futures. They also filed for copper. Not launching single-stock perpetuals "at this time." Seems inevitable though considering that single-stock 15-minute markets are an ambition for the firm. Kalshi's head of… Prediction markets uninvited from White House tech party Prediction market executives appear to have been scratched from today’s White House card. Semafor reporter Eleanor Mueller says a White House official confirmed prediction market companies will not participate in President Trump’s event with tech leaders, despite earlier reporting that Kalshi and its backer Paradigm were among those expected to attend. The gathering is intended to promote America’s “innovative and technological dominance,” with crypto heavyweights reportedly in the mix. Why prediction markets are suddenly sitting this one out isn’t clear. But after seemingly making the guest list last week, Kalshi and company will apparently have to watch this particular market from the sidelines. 👀 "The President will host an event with tech leaders tomorrow to strengthen America’s innovative and technological dominance," a White House official tells me. "Prediction market companies will not be a part of the event." https://t.co/GAfXAbcbFS Connecticut tells appeals court: not so fast, Kalshi Connecticut isn’t ready to let Kalshi hit the pause button on state enforcement. According to attorney Daniel Wallach, the state is urging the Second Circuit to reject Kalshi’s request for interim administrative relief while the prediction market operator pursues an emergency injunction pending appeal. Connecticut has until August 24 to formally oppose that motion. Connecticut urges Second Circuit to deny Kalshi’s request for interim administrative relief, which would bar state enforcement action until the resolution of Kalshi’s emergency motion for an injunction pending appeal, and give the State until Aug. 24th to object to the motion. pic.twitter.com/KT3g7ms0zf — Daniel Wallach (@WALLACHLEGAL) August 18, 2026 Kalshi exec goes to Harvard on prediction market insider trading Kalshi's Robert DeNault has co-authored a new piece with Wharton professor Daniel Taylor for the Harvard Law School Forum on Corporate Governance, examining how insider-trading surveillance in prediction markets differs from traditional securities markets. The timing is certainly lively. With politicians increasingly raising alarms about suspiciously well-informed prediction market traders, the industry is facing growing scrutiny over who knows what, and when. New piece by @ProfAnalytics and myself, published today by @HarvardCorpGov, about the ways insider trading surveillance in prediction markets differs from traditional securities markets. Give it a read if you're interested in the PM surveillance space - link below. pic.twitter.com/ff5HyP93oE Kalshi pushes back as Congress targets wildfire prediction markets Congress is now looking to put out the fire on wildfire prediction markets, with a new House bill seeking to ban contracts tied to wildfires and other natural disasters. Kalshi’s Robert J. Denault, however, would like everyone to know his company isn’t holding the matches. Responding to Senator Adam Schiff’s criticism of wildfire wagering, Denault said Kalshi doesn’t list wildfire or war markets, arguing they create “bad incentives” and are inconsistent with federal commodities law. In other words: prediction markets are catching heat, and Kalshi wants everyone to check whose kitchen the smoke is coming from. Kalshi doesn’t list war or wildfire markets because they create bad incentives and are inconsistent with the CEA. Just like one politician doesn’t define everyone in Washington, one offshore prediction market doesn’t define the whole industry. https://t.co/DMdYQIU8BM — robertjdenault (@robertjdenault) August 18, 2026

item.title: Crypto.com and Washington officials seek pause as Ninth Circuit weighs event-contract appeals
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite Score: 4.14
Crypto.com and Washington state officials want to put their federal court fight over event contracts on hold while the Ninth Circuit weighs appeals that could resolve the key legal question between them. North American Derivatives Exchange Inc., which does business as OG and is referred to here as Crypto.com, filed the joint request Tuesday (August 18) with Washington Attorney General Nicholas W. Brown and officials from the Washington State Gambling Commission. If the court approves the arrangement, state officials would temporarily hold off on certain civil or criminal enforcement involving Crypto.com and event contracts traded on federally regulated Designated Contract Markets, known as DCMs. Both sides say continuing the Washington litigation now could waste time and money when the appeals court is already considering the same underlying question. They agreed that “good cause exists to grant their requested relief to prevent unnecessary expenditure of judicial resources and the Parties’ resources while the related issues are before the Ninth Circuit.” Crypto.com brought the Washington case on July 22, challenging the possibility that state officials could enforce Washington gambling and consumer laws against its event-contract activity. Crypto.com contends federal regulation under the Commodity Exchange Act displaces state law for contracts traded on DCMs. The filing says the company “has alleged that all state laws are preempted as they relate to trading of event contracts on DCMs” because of the federal law. Ninth Circuit Crypto.com ruling could determine whether federal law overrides Washington gambling rules Three Nevada cases involving North American Derivatives Exchange, Kalshi and Robinhood Derivatives LLC are already before the Ninth Circuit. Briefing is complete, and judges heard arguments April 16. The Washington parties say those cases raise the same federal preemption question. While the pause remains in place, Washington officials would refrain from enforcement under the Consumer Protection Act, Gambling Act, Recovery of Money Lost at Gambling Act and other state laws tied to Crypto.com’s DCM event-contract transactions. The federal case would also be administratively stayed. After the relevant Ninth Circuit proceedings end, both sides would meet within 10 days to discuss what happens next. Unless they reach another agreement, they would submit a status report within 20 days outlining how they believe the appellate ruling changes the Washington case. The proposal would not end their wider disagreement. As the filing states, “this stipulation does not resolve any claim or defense asserted in this action.” The dispute comes amid a wider fight over who regulates prediction markets. Washington’s Gambling Commission said in December 2025 that event-based prediction markets were unauthorized in the state. In July, a coalition of 44 state attorneys general also urged the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to withdraw and rewrite a proposed prediction-markets rule, arguing sports wagering remains primarily a state responsibility. The agreement includes an 18-month backstop. If no further court order arrives by then, Washington officials could leave the arrangement after giving Crypto.com 14 days’ written notice. The parties submitted the stipulated motion and proposed order to U.S. Magistrate Judge Brian A. Tsuchida. Featured image: Crypto.com / Canva

item.title: Connecticut judge rejects Kalshi bid to pause gambling enforcement during appeal
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite Score: 4.08
A federal judge in Connecticut will allow state officials to keep enforcing gambling laws against prediction-market operator Kalshi while the company takes its case to an appeals court. U.S. District Judge Vernon D. Oliver turned down Kalshi’s emergency bid for an injunction pending appeal on August 15. He also denied its backup request for temporary administrative relief while Kalshi asks the Second Circuit for an injunction. The latest order, which has been reviewed by ReadWrite, followed Oliver’s August 10 decision denying a preliminary injunction against Connecticut officials and the Department of Consumer Protection. Kalshi appealed that ruling before returning to Oliver three days later for protection from enforcement during the appeal. Oliver had concluded that Kalshi’s sports-event contracts do not qualify as “swaps” under the Commodity Exchange Act, putting them outside the Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s exclusive jurisdiction. He also found that federal law does not displace Connecticut’s longstanding power to regulate sports wagering. Kalshi faces higher hurdle during Connecticut appeal Getting an injunction during an appeal requires Kalshi to make a stronger case for likely success than it needed for preliminary relief. Oliver found the company had not cleared that higher threshold. Several arguments again challenged his conclusions about swaps and federal preemption, with Kalshi saying the Second Circuit could reach a different result. “While the Second Circuit may ultimately ‘disagree with certain features of this Court’s decision,’ the possibility for reversal alone (a possibility that exists in every appeal) does not warrant the extraordinary measure of injunctive relief,” Oliver wrote. Oliver likewise found that unsettled law and differing decisions elsewhere were not enough. “A split in caselaw outside of this Circuit does not justify injunctive relief pending appeal, nor does the sheer fact that this is an issue of first impression,” Oliver wrote. Kalshi also cited CFTC guidance issued August 11 after New York’s attorney general sued over its event contracts. The agency declared a “market emergency” and instructed Kalshi to keep its exchange operating normally even if a New York state court ordered otherwise. Oliver found that directive did not alter his earlier conclusion about the contracts falling outside exclusive CFTC jurisdiction. Kalshi also argued that Connecticut enforcement could expose it to civil or criminal liability, while compliance could mean shutting trading to Connecticut customers and suffering financial and reputational damage. Oliver again found those concerns insufficient, including what he viewed as speculative risks of CFTC action. “Kalshi has not provided a sufficiently compelling basis to further restrict Connecticut’s enforcement of its gambling regulatory regime during the pendency of the appeal,” Oliver wrote. The dispute began after Kalshi expanded into sports contracts in January 2025. By a February 2026 hearing, those products accounted for 80% to 90% of its listed contracts and revenue, while the company was valued around $11 billion. Connecticut sent Kalshi a cease-and-desist letter in December 2025. Commissioner Bryan T. Cafferelli said, “Only licensed entities may offer sports wagering in the state of Connecticut. None of these entities possesses a license to offer wagering in our state, and even if they did, their contracts violate numerous other state laws and policies, including offering wagers to individuals under the age of 21.” Oliver ultimately found that neither the equities nor public interest supported blocking enforcement. Meanwhile, Gov. Ned Lamont’s proposed Bill No. 5038, which would have added prediction-market safeguards and required a statewide study, has died in committee. Featured image: Kalshi / Canva

item.title: Live Five: The Midnight Pine, Elizabeth Bowersox, Morricone Youth, Michele Lundeen, International Pop Overthrow
item.description:
Source: San Diego Reader stories Score: 4.48
The Midnight Pine at the Music Box August 21 The Midnight Pine came out of the gate running at full speed when their full-length Awake Now took home the trophy for Best Local Recording at the 2013 San Diego Music Awards and their 2014 album Buried won a SDMA for Best Americana Album. Their song "Caution" was heard on the Bravo TV show Girlfriends' Guide to Divorce. The band recently released a new vinyl pressing of their 2020 full-length Live At A.D. The Midnight Pine presents Buried: The Final Midnight marks their farewell performance. According to the band, “For this Final Midnight we will be celebrating our work and dedication with one last big show. We will be playing all of Buried, the second record, [and] lots of familiar songs we played often as well as some songs we have never played live. And there are some special secret guests that will be gracing the stage.” The bill includes indie art-rock and cinematic folk band The Color Forty Nine, which utilizes unique setups including baritone ukuleles, custom effects-pedal violins, Casiotones, and cinematic brass arrangements. International Pop Overthrow at Black Cat Bar August 21 and 22 Named after the debut album by the power pop band Material Issue, the International Pop Overthrow music festival was founded in 1998 by L.A. music writer and pop fan David Bash. Initially a ten-day event featuring around 120 acts across a handful of Los Angeles venues, the event expanded over the decades to various US cities (such as Chicago, New York, and Atlanta) and international locations like Vancouver, Toronto, Stockholm, and Glasgow. Each edition is intended to celebrate melodic rock and power pop, giving a global stage to unsigned grassroots artists alongside occasional major acts. This year’s local edition features multiple bands over two nights, all playing short sets punctuated by quick transitions between acts, with the overall emphasis on melodic, hook-filled music. Over a dozen independent, underground, and unsigned bands are scheduled to perform. Friday, August 21 features Grammy nominated family rocker Ralph Covert, Mess of Fun, Scott Samuels and Friends, Tamar Berk, Hector Penalosa, and Super Buffet, Saturday’s bill includes Suite 100, True Stories, Michael Culhane,The Colour Monday, Courtney McKenna, The Rightovers, and power jangle-rock trio The Glimmer Stars. Elizabeth Bowersox at Carlsbad City Library Schulman Auditorium August 22 Front Row Saturday brings audiences an intimate experience in the state-of-the-art Ruby G. Schulman Auditorium, spotlighting national touring performers as well as emerging local talents. This edition featured acoustic country artist Elizabeth Bowersox, dubbed by Coastal Reverb as “One of San Diego’s most prolific up-and-coming songwriters.” A classically trained vocalist with a rock and roll edge, her music fuses folk, country, and unapologetic pop. Her debut EP California Queen earned her a 2026 San Diego Music Award for Best Country or Americana Album. She recently released a single for her twangy track “Red Hot Summer,” and a new video is streaming online with her song “The Last Girl” performed live at Big Bear Lake.
